changeSet.author: restaurantos-agent
changeSet.comment: Resolve any (tenant_id, lower(email)) duplicates deterministically before the unique index is created, so a database with real data cannot fail the migration.

changeSet.author: restaurantos-agent
changeSet.comment: Fail loudly, naming row-level security, if the repair did not converge — rather than leaving an operator to deduce it from an index violation.

changeSet.author: restaurantos-agent
changeSet.comment: Per-tenant, case-insensitive email uniqueness over live rows — enforced by the database so a race cannot pass it.
changeSet.sql:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uk_users_tenant_email_ci ON users (tenant_id, lower(email)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
-- Supporting index for the tenant user list (13-11). The list is always tenant-scoped, -- optionally filtered on is_active, and always sorted by (email, id) so a page boundary -- is stable. uk_users_tenant_email already serves the unfiltered sort; this one serves -- the filtered sort without a re-sort, and its leading columns match the filter exactly. -- -- No index is added for the search term. Search is a case-insensitive CONTAINS over -- email and full name, which has a leading wildcard and cannot use a b-tree; the honest -- alternative is a pg_trgm GIN index, and installing an extension is not something this -- changeset does silently. The scan it falls back to is bounded by one tenant's user -- count and by a hard page-size cap, which is the mitigation for T-13-11-H. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_tenant_active_email ON users (tenant_id, is_active, email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

rollback.sql: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uk_users_tenant_email_ci; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_users_tenant_active_email;
